title: Finite reduction of the completed map
statement:
For every $n$, reduction of $\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] modulo $I^n$, conjugated by
the canonical reduction isomorphisms, is exactly
$$
 \Ex_{\square,K_n}:Lg_n^*Rf_*K_n
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg_n'^*K_n.
$$
These reduction squares commute with $n+1\to n$ and with compatible
endomorphisms.

note:
*Source note:* the reduction of the completed pullback is the formula
$Lf^*_{comp}M=\Rlim Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ of
Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), whose $n$-th level is
$Lf_n^*$ of the $n$-th level; Stacks states the formula for the completed
pullback of one object of $D(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$, whereas the displayed
statement reduces the completed base-change exchange map of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], which the verified entries
do not construct, and the blueprint adds that reduction together with its
compatibility with the transitions and with compatible endomorphisms.

proof.text:
Use the datum of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], with $n\geq1$, and its first identification $s_A:S\xrightarrow{\sim}A_\infty$ before $H$, its direct-image comparison $d:T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_\infty$, and $\xi=\Ex^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$. Thus $d\xi=V'Hs_A$. Write $c:C_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ for the ordered map $\chi$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square]. To justify its reduction edges without assuming completeness of ordinary pullback, put $N=Lg^*Rf_*K$ and $M=Rf'_*Lg'^*K$. By [def-weil-pbc-four-corners] the towers $A_\bullet,C_\bullet$ are the strict reduction towers of $N,M$, with the canonical pullback/tensor identifications on $A_\bullet$. For ANY $Z\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_{Y'}))$, set $Z_n=Z\otimes^L_{A_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'}$ and $\widehat Z=\Rlim Z_\bullet$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to $\operatorname{Sh}(Y'_{\Proet})$. It identifies $\operatorname{Res}(Z)_n$ with $Z_n$, identifies their derived limits and completion units, and identifies the two finite reductions of $\widehat Z$. Now apply [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] to the arbitrary constant-coefficient complex $\operatorname{Res}(Z)$ with $\Lambda=A$, in [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Noetherianity, finite generation of $I$, torsion $A/I$, and perfection of $P_n$ follow from our adic datum. Transport its projection-induced functorial isomorphism through the preceding canonical comparisons to obtain
$$\rho_{Z,n}:\widehat Z\otimes^L_{A_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'}\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_n.$$
The projection to $Z_n$ is preserved by the limit comparison, so this is precisely the projection-induced reduction map, not an arbitrary isomorphism. In particular $q_{C,n}=\rho_{M,n}$ exists for the possibly incomplete $M$. The same construction on $N$ gives $q_{A,n}$; under $s_A$ this is the canonical finite reduction of [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], since both are induced by evaluation to $A_n$. Consequently the prescribed edges of [def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square] are $\sigma_n=q_{A,n}(s_A\otimes1)$, $\tau_n=q_{C,n}(c^{-1}\otimes1)$, $\alpha_n=h_n\sigma_n$, and $\delta_n=h'_n\tau_n$. This repairs that definition's attribution of $\rho_{M,n}$ to a complete-input reconstruction lemma: we prove its existence using the arbitrary-input reduction theorem instead.

proof.text: The ordered composite defining $c=\chi$ in [def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square] is $c=\lambda_E^{-1}\Rlim_m(\pi_{f',E,P_m})$, where $E=Lg'^*K$. Under the level identifications of [def-weil-pbc-four-corners], the maps $\pi_{f',E,P_m}$ are precisely $h'_m$ of [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows]. Their tower morphism is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility]. The comparison $\lambda_E$ is the very comparison $d$ specified in [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], since both use the tower $E\otimes^LP_m=Lg_m'^*K_m$ and the canonical comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Therefore $c=d^{-1}H'$ and $dc=dd^{-1}H'=H'$. This is an identity of ordered composites, not uniqueness of a triangle filler. Now [lem-weil-pbc-rectangle-derived-limit] gives $V'H=H'V$, so $d\xi=H'Vs_A=dcVs_A$. Cancelling the specified isomorphism $d$ gives $\xi=cVs_A$.

proof.text:
Let $e:N\to M$ be the ambient exchange map. By [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows], $v_n$ is exactly $e\otimes1$ under the canonical identification of $N_n$ with $A_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility] these are its compatible reduction-tower maps, and their image under [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] is $V:A_\infty\to C_\infty$. The arbitrary-input projection-induced isomorphisms of [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] are functorial in the input complex. The scalar comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] is canonical and preserves the towers, finite reductions and units. Apply that functoriality to $\operatorname{Res}(e)$ and identify the two sides through those comparisons. This gives
$$q_{C,n}(V\otimes1)=v_nq_{A,n}.$$
In particular this use of functoriality has no completeness hypothesis on $M$ or $N$. Tensoring step 2 and substituting step 1 now gives
$$\tau_n\overline\xi_n=q_{C,n}(c^{-1}\otimes1)(c\otimes1)(V\otimes1)(s_A\otimes1)=v_nq_{A,n}(s_A\otimes1)=v_n\sigma_n.$$
The finite equality in [lem-weil-pbc-rectangle-derived-limit] is $h'_nv_n=v'_nh_n$, whence
$$\delta_n\overline\xi_n=h'_nv_n\sigma_n=v'_nh_n\sigma_n=v'_n\alpha_n.$$
The maps $\sigma_n,\tau_n$ are isomorphisms by step 1, and $h_n,h'_n$ are the specified projection-formula isomorphisms of [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows]. Therefore $\delta_n\overline\xi_n\alpha_n^{-1}=v'_n$, precisely the specified finite-level exchange isomorphism.

proof.text:
Let $r^S_{n+1,n}=1_S\otimes(P_{n+1}\to P_n)$ and $r^T_{n+1,n}=1_T\otimes(P_{n+1}\to P_n)$, viewed in the ambient $A$-coefficient category. For either $Z=N,M$ the quotient-tower completion unit $\eta_Z:Z\to\widehat Z$ has projection to $Z_n$ equal to the scalar-extension unit. Hence the projection-induced $\rho_{Z,n}$ of [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction], transported through the unit-preserving comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], satisfies $\rho_{Z,n}(\eta_Z\otimes1)=1_{Z_n}$. Since $\rho_{Z,n}$ is an isomorphism by step 1, $\eta_Z\otimes1=\rho_{Z,n}^{-1}$. Naturality of tensoring the fixed map $\eta_Z$ with the quotient map gives $r^{\widehat Z}_{n+1,n}(\eta_Z\otimes1_{P_{n+1}})=(\eta_Z\otimes1_{P_n})r^Z_{n+1,n}$. Multiplying by the two inverses gives $r^Z_{n+1,n}\rho_{Z,n+1}=\rho_{Z,n}r^{\widehat Z}_{n+1,n}$. For $Z=N$ compose with $s_A\otimes1$, and for $Z=M$ compose with $c^{-1}\otimes1$; tensor naturality of these fixed maps gives $a_{n+1,n}\sigma_{n+1}=\sigma_nr^S_{n+1,n}$ and $c_{n+1,n}\tau_{n+1}=\tau_nr^T_{n+1,n}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility], $b_{n+1,n}h_{n+1}=h_na_{n+1,n}$, $d_{n+1,n}h'_{n+1}=h'_nc_{n+1,n}$ and $d_{n+1,n}v'_{n+1}=v'_nb_{n+1,n}$. Substitution gives
$$
 b_{n+1,n}\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_nr^S_{n+1,n},\qquad
 d_{n+1,n}\delta_{n+1}=\delta_nr^T_{n+1,n}.
$$
Finally, tensor functoriality gives $r^T_{n+1,n}\overline\xi_{n+1}=\overline\xi_nr^S_{n+1,n}$. These three equations and the equation for $v'$ exhibit the compatibility on every edge of the two reduction squares. This is ambient transition compatibility, not an assertion that tensoring over $A$ with $P_n$ is the same as normalized reduction over $P_{n+1}$.

For a compatible endomorphism of $K$, use its induced corner maps $u_{A,n},u_{B,n},u_{C,n},u_{D,n}$ and their limits $u_{A,\infty},u_{B,\infty},u_{C,\infty},u_{D,\infty}$. The finite operator equations of [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility] include $h_nu_{A,n}=u_{B,n}h_n$, $h'_nu_{C,n}=u_{D,n}h'_n$, $v'_nu_{B,n}=u_{D,n}v'_n$ and $v_nu_{A,n}=u_{C,n}v_n$. Applying [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] gives $Hu_{A,\infty}=u_{B,\infty}H$, $H'u_{C,\infty}=u_{D,\infty}H'$, $V'u_{B,\infty}=u_{D,\infty}V'$ and $Vu_{A,\infty}=u_{C,\infty}V$. Functoriality of completed pullback [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] identifies $s_Au_S=u_{A,\infty}s_A$; the canonical comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] gives $du_T=u_{D,\infty}d$. Since $c=d^{-1}H'$, it follows that $cu_{C,\infty}=u_Tc$. Apply the arbitrary-input functorial reduction of [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction], with the canonical coefficient comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], to the induced endomorphisms of $N$ and $M$. Their quotient towers give $u_{A,n}$ and $u_{C,n}$, and their limits give $u_{A,\infty}$ and $u_{C,\infty}$. Thus $q_{A,n}(u_{A,\infty}\otimes1)=u_{A,n}q_{A,n}$ and $q_{C,n}(u_{C,\infty}\otimes1)=u_{C,n}q_{C,n}$, without a completeness assumption on $M$. Substitution gives $\sigma_n(u_S\otimes1)=u_{A,n}\sigma_n$ and $\tau_n(u_T\otimes1)=u_{C,n}\tau_n$, hence $\alpha_n(u_S\otimes1)=u_{B,n}\alpha_n$ and $\delta_n(u_T\otimes1)=u_{D,n}\delta_n$. Finally step 2 gives $\xi u_S=cVu_{A,\infty}s_A=cu_{C,\infty}Vs_A=u_T\xi$. Tensoring this equality gives $\overline\xi_n(u_S\otimes1)=(u_T\otimes1)\overline\xi_n$; the lower-edge equation is $v'_nu_{B,n}=u_{D,n}v'_n$. These four edge equations prove operator compatibility of the square.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every $n$, the diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
S\otimes^LP_n @>{\overline\xi_n}>> T\otimes^LP_n\\
@V{\alpha_n}V{\sim}V @VV{\delta_n}V{\sim}\\
B_n @>{v'_n}>> D_n
\end{CD}
$$

commutes. Hence reduction of
$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ modulo $I^n$, conjugated
by the displayed canonical reduction isomorphisms, is exactly the S8
transported finite-level exchange map $v'_n=\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}$.
The squares for $n+1\to n$ commute, and the assertion is natural for
compatible tower endomorphisms. Under a Frobenius-equivariant datum, use
$\Phi_{Y'}P_n=P_n$ to give the two reductions their induced Weil structures.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_n(\Theta_S\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\alpha_n),\\
\delta_n(\Theta_T\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\delta_n),
\end{aligned}
$$

and the displayed reduction square is a square of Weil objects.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Under $S=A_\infty$ and the direct-image completion identification
$T\simeq C_\infty$, the completed exchange map is both limit composites

$$
V'H=H'V:A_\infty\longrightarrow D_\infty,
$$

followed by the inverse of direct-image/limit commutation. More explicitly,
if $d:T\to D_\infty$ is direct-image/limit commutation and
$c:C_\infty\to T$ is direct-image completion, then its construction gives
$dc=H'$. Functorial finite
reduction and the component equations of the limit rectangle give

$$
\tau_n\overline\xi_n=v_n\sigma_n.
$$

Consequently the two composites around the completed reduction square are

$$
\delta_n\overline\xi_n
=h'_n\tau_n\overline\xi_n=h'_nv_n\sigma_n
$$

and

$$
v'_n\alpha_n=v'_nh_n\sigma_n.
$$

They are equal term by term because $h'_nv_n=v'_nh_n$ in the finite-level
rectangle. Naturality of finite reduction makes $\sigma_n$ and $\tau_n$
commute with $n+1\to n$, and functoriality of tensor reduction does the same
for $\overline\xi_n$. Together with the four transition equations, this
shows that the completed squares commute with $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ on every
corner. The limit construction and all four reduction edges are
operator-equivariant, so the conjugated equality is operator-natural as well.

For Frobenius, the definition of $\Theta_S$ transports
$\Theta_{A,\infty}$ across $s$, and the $n$th product-cone component followed
by $h_n$ is $\alpha_n$. This gives the first displayed Weil equation. The
definition of $\Theta_T$ transports $\Theta_{D,\infty}$ across $t$, and its
$n$th component is $\delta_n$, giving the second. The completed Frobenius
equation for $\overline\xi_n$, together with finite-level equivariance of
$v'_n$, now says that every arrow of the reduction square is a Weil morphism.

No extra hypothesis, no statement change, no new node.
